name: ShadowSyndicate
keyCapabilities: Advanced Data Exfiltration to third-party clouds
Core infrastructure sharing across ransomware gangs
Credential theft via LSASS and NTDS.dit extraction
recommendedActions: Block and alert on specific SSH fingerprints identified in known RaaS infrastructures.
Implement MFA Number Matching or more rigorous push notification limits to counter 'MFA Fatigue' attacks.
Filter and block outgoing traffic to reputationally suspicious file-hosting sites like MEGA, S3 buckets with uncommon headers, and Slack/Discord webhooks for non-standard purposes.
Disable the use of unauthorized Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools like TeamViewer or AnyDesk on internal endpoints.
Proactively patch public-facing applications against CVE-2021-35464 and other high-risk infrastructure vulnerabilities.
Restrict access to internal documentation repositories (SharePoint/Teams) containing technical network maps or credentials.
Implement heavy monitoring for 'living off the land' binaries like mshta.exe, rundll32.exe, and regsvr32.exe.
Conduct automated hunting for Ryuk, Cl0p, and ALPHV-related indicators across all segments.
campaignsText: ShadowSyndicate has shown a consistent operational rhythm since late 2022, frequently rotating infrastructure to support various ransomware campaigns such as Quantum (late 2022), Nokoyawa (late 2022), and ALPHV (early 2023). Their campaign pattern is defined by heavy 'multi-tenant' usage, where a single cluster of servers may host tools for multiple different ransomware brands. They have shown an increasing effort in targeting high-value targets in the manufacturing and critical infrastructure sectors throughout 2024.
description: ShadowSyndicate is a highly sophisticated Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) affiliate known for its extensive infrastructure exploitation and ability to operate across multiple ransomware families including Cl0p, ALPHV, and Ryuk. They utilize a 'double extortion' model, combining high-volume data theft with heavy encryption of critical systems.
goals: ShadowSyndicate primarily operates for financial gain via a double extortion methodology, where sensitive data is exfiltrated prior to the deployment of ransomware. Their target profile is exceptionally broad, including critical infrastructure, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and education across global markets. They specifically prioritize high-value targets containing proprietary intellectual property, such as source code or internal guidance documents, which can be used as additional leverage during negotiations.
